settled.decided: python3 -m unittest from the invoicer folder, as tests/__init__.py gives it and pyproject.toml and the README give none. All 78 tests passed before any change, and all 86 after each step.

settled.about: where the invoice's currency is kept
settled.decided: INVOICE_CURRENCY in render, the module that writes it after each amount, as render's default; the sheet reader imports it for its refusal of other currencies, as it already imported from invoicer.tax, and its own copy is gone. render keeps its currency parameter, as the package offers render.

settled.about: where rounding to the cent is kept
settled.decided: round_to_cent in invoicer.tax, beside CENT, which tax_of and the sheet reader's price both call in place of two quantize calls.
The refusals of a sheet with no lines and of a header row lacking a column take Description, Price, and Quantity from _HEADERS; their texts are byte for byte as before, as the existing tests show.
The docstring says a currency other than the invoice's, so it still holds when render's currency changes.

settled.about: why a cell's paragraphs are joined by a space
settled.decided: A comment says Calc saves each line of a cell typed on several lines as a paragraph, joined so the description prints as one invoice row.

settled.about: why the OSError is dropped from the refusal
settled.decided: A comment beside from None says the refusal names the system's reason itself.

settled.about: why the column letters count from 1
settled.decided: A comment says Calc's letters have none for zero, so each turn takes 1 before divmod, column 25 being Z and 26 AA.

settled.about: the tests of the reader's behaviours
settled.decided: Each pins what the code gives today, by the existing helpers formatted_as_text and wrong_quantity where they fit, and by raw rows where Calc saves a cell that the list rows can't make: two paragraphs, a percent cell, 25 repeated columns. The path that can't be opened is the test's own folder, as a file without read permission still opens for root.
